correctness.rationale: For every m>=3 and positive real spoke weight, hub best response is z<=m/2. Direct comparison of two rim actions shows zeros need two opposite rim neighbors if and only if lambda<=2, and ones cannot have two equal rim neighbors if lambda<2. Thus the complete equilibrium configurations are cyclic gap lengths 2 or 3 below threshold, isolated zeros including empty at threshold, and all-one rim above. Starting-zero double counting yields the refined binomial formulas. A three-state transfer trace proves the Perrin recurrence and the cycle independent-set trace proves Lucas. Strictness is settled by equality cases. All welfare levels follow from exactly 2z rim-cut edges and m-z spoke-cut edges. A direct one-zero flip argument proves the exact global optimum, and the minimum PNE value is realized at ceil(m/3). The exact-rational checker reproduced 72 full cases and 393120 profiles and independently checked sequence counts to 299; these checks support the infinite proof rather than replacing it.

originality.rationale: The complete parametric wheel census is not obtained by renaming the known Perrin or Lucas sequences: the fresh conclusion is that a single natural spoke-to-rim weight threshold separates Perrin, Lucas, and two-equilibrium phases, with exact refined counts, strictness, all welfare levels and sharp inefficiency. Full primary text on ladder/circular-ladder anti-coordination (arXiv:2101.09103), graphical anti-coordination equilibrium existence and dynamics (arXiv:2301.02889), and binary polymatrix welfare complexity (arXiv:2311.03195) supplies related definitions and motivation but not this full theorem; unlike the wheel, a circular ladder has no universal hub. Multiple directed searches of weighted local-max cuts, zero-temperature spin-flip stable configurations, wheel Nash counts and exact tables found no stronger covering result. This is a best-knowledge originality assessment, not proof of publication uniqueness.
residual_risks: A less discoverable result in zero-temperature anti-ferromagnetic Ising metastability or local-optimal-cut enumeration might give the same weighted-wheel result under different language.
Searches cannot establish absolute uniqueness; an unindexed exact transfer-matrix enumeration with a wheel hub might dominate some components.

value.rationale: The wheel is a natural hub-and-ring network with heterogeneous degree and uniform tunable hub influence. The full infinite-family phase diagram answers a motivated quantitative question for strategic substitutes: how the strength of hub ties changes equilibrium abundance, robustness to tie-breaking, and welfare loss. The coexistence of exponentially many equilibria below lambda=2, an even larger Lucas-number tie phase at lambda=2, and only two strict equilibria above provides a sharp structural phenomenon, not an arbitrary finite census. The exact price-of-anarchy formula shows a nontrivial worst-equilibrium welfare penalty (unweighted limit 9/8), while all equilibria at lambda>=2 are efficient. It does not claim a general-network theorem or more than the specified network game.
